_about: Print settings for the v6 parts, read by cad/slice.py. Values are OrcaSlicer's own keys and value formats (filament keys are lists). Layering: the system presets named here, then 'process'/'filament', then 'supports' (or enable_support 0), then the part's 'settings'. 'plates' are parts printed together, sliced into one project; one process slices a plate, so its parts share supports and settings, and the plate holds its own 'copies'. cad/slice.py writes 'orient', 'copies' and 'settings' back here when a project was saved from the GUI. Spec: cad/PRINT_LIST.md, Global print settings + Supports are the slicer's job. 'variants' are parts of a non-default build (e.g. HIP_YOKE_VARIANT=glued) that the default table leaves out; cad/slice.py --variant <name> slices them.

feet.note: both feet on one plate, sole down

hip_yoke_glued.note: HIP_YOKE_VARIANT=glued: the hip yoke as two support-free U-channels, snapped and glued (cad/v6/hip_yoke_glued.py)

hip_yoke_glued_roll.note: on edge, model -Y (the y -10 bed face) down; no supports, no brim

hip_yoke_glued_pitch.note: on its back, model -X (the x -14 bed face) down; no supports, no brim

ankle_link_glued.note: ANKLE_LINK_VARIANT=glued: the ankle link as a conformal cradle and a fork, printed without supports, snapped and glued (cad/v6/ankle_link_glued.py)

ankle_link_glued_cradle.note: bottom down (the four walls' flat bottom); no supports, no brim

ankle_link_glued_fork.note: on edge, model -Y (the y -14.5 face) down; no supports, no brim

ankle_link.note: on its back (model +X up), the rear tine on the bed: the grip screws' teardrop roofs assume print-up = model +X (ankle_link.py). Supports under the web and the front tine

arm_fore_v6_L.note: on its back, web face down

arm_fore_v6_R.note: on its back, web face down

arm_upper_v6_L.note: on its back, web face down

arm_upper_v6_R.note: on its back, web face down

head_face.note: flat, outer (+X) face down, camera bosses up; the outer-face pocket is then a ~50 x 44 mm ceiling 1.8 mm up, so supports (PRINT_LIST says none: open question). head.py PRINT_ORIENT_FACE = eye(3) stands it on edge; the STL is in the assembly frame

hip_yoke_v6.note: on edge, model -Y on the bed; 5 mm outer brim

leg_link_v6.note: on its back, web face on the bed

yaw_bearing_housing.note: the face against the pelvis down

yaw_carrier_v6.note: horn-plate face down, bay walls rising; the lip's 1.1 mm ledge prints unsupported, so its face that stops the bearing's inner race carries no support interface
